clue.text: Henry and have headgear which is a disadvantage

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Henry and have headgear which is a disadvantage' lacks the I that HANDICAP (H + AND + I + CAP) needs; no scan, and a search of the text found no fuller version
annotationWithheld.clue: Henry and have headgear which is a disadvantage

clue.text: Prize the opposite of peace in our time

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the abbreviation for our era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
war is the opposite of peace

explanation.surface: A remark that a prize brings the reverse of peace in our time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peace in our time' is Chamberlain's famous 1938 phrase, which hides that 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize or honour given for achievement.

clue.text: Curiously angled yours in a menacing way

indicators.note: curiously suggests the letters are arranged in an odd, unexpected way

explanation.surface: A strangely bent shape of yours looks threatening.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting dangerously means doing so with threat or peril, which is menace.

clue.text: Having a head, so cover it over tea

parts.note: to cap is to cover the top of something

indicators.note: over here signals the letters of the word tea being turned over and reworked

explanation.surface: Having a head, you should put a lid on it during teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' makes ATE, the anagram of TEA. 'so' is only a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitate is a botanical and anatomical term for something ending in a knob or head-like cluster.

clue.text: Family openly acknowledged? They improve the image

parts.note: something public is openly known and acknowledged
one's relations are one's family

explanation.surface: A family openly acknowledged, and the spin doctors polishing its image.
explanation.walkthrough: Family openly acknowledged gives relations that are public, so the two words swap places in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: PR people manage a company's reputation, working to present it favourably.

clue.text: Mean to have journalist left inside with salesman

indicators.note: inside signals that the journalist and left go within the word for mean

parts.note: par is an average or norm, so a mean
ED, editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A stingy person keeps a reporter on the left with a travelling seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' suggests stingy; here it is the average, PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is an itinerant trader selling small goods door to door.

clue.text: Turn up during concert for a bit of persecution

indicators.note: during signals that one piece occurs within the concert word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at London's summer Proms season

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for turn is read bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone shows up at a concert for a spot of harassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the turn word to make OG. 'Turn up' reads as one verb meaning arrive, which hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogrom is an organised massacre or campaign of violence against a persecuted group.

clue.text: Party with new fellow

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A party with a new chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a fellow or tutor at a university college, especially Oxford or Cambridge.

clue.text: Stories of how an ace doesn't change

indicators.note: change signals that the letters are altered into a different order

explanation.surface: Tales of how a top player never alters.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ACE and DOESN'T (dropping the apostrophe) rearrange; 'of how an' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotes are short entertaining accounts of incidents, a kind of tale.

clue.text: Can't manage a quiet snatch of sleep

indicators.note: manage suggests handling the letters of the word can't and reorganising them

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Unable to get even a brief, quiet doze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manage' rearranges CAN'T into CATN, with the apostrophe ignored. 'Can't manage' reads as a single phrase meaning fail, which hides that 'manage' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short light sleep, a brief doze.

clue.text: One who starts to mix gin in beer — not I!

indicators.note: to mix signals combining and reordering the letters of gin in beer, with the I taken away as the clue says

explanation.surface: A novice tries mixing gin into beer, but says 'not me!'
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GIN IN BEER, minus one I ('not I'), rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or newcomer is someone starting out at something.

clue.text: A marginal advantage

parts.note: a slight lead over rivals, but also playing on the word marginal as being at the border or brink of something

explanation.definitionFit: Having the slight superiority over a rival is being ahead, and the rim of anything is its margin.

clue.text: Well fitted to follow, having roamed around

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them

indicators.note: around signals that the letters of roamed are moved about

explanation.surface: Something fitting nicely trails after a wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the wanderer's word into ORMADE. 'to' and 'having' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit made to measure fits perfectly, and figuratively ideally suited.

clue.text: Greeted by mad emcee, low in arrangement

indicators.note: in arrangement tells us the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Welcomed by a crazed compère who sinks into ordering things.
explanation.definitionFit: To be greeted warmly is to be received hospitably on arrival.

clue.text: Fraudulent person may claim to be Bill

parts.note: someone claiming an identity says I'm
a bill is a poster or placard, as in billposter

explanation.surface: A con artist might claim to be called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but here it means a placard. Saying 'I'm a poster' is claiming to be a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposter is a fraud who pretends to be someone else.

clue.text: Record of small picture

parts.note: micro means very small
a film is a motion picture

explanation.surface: A record of a little photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Microfilm stores documents as tiny photographic images, a medium for keeping records.

clue.text: The obligation of tax

explanation.definitionFit: Duty is both a moral or legal commitment and a levy charged on goods.

clue.text: Bypassing police trap, full of blackcurrant drink

indicators.note: full of signals that the police trap holds the drink inside

parts.note: a sting is an undercover police operation to catch criminals
kir is white wine mixed with blackcurrant liqueur (cassis)

explanation.surface: Avoiding a police set-up while loaded with a fruity aperitif.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirting something means going around its edge, avoiding it.

clue.text: Does something as court goes in

indicators.note: goes in signals that the court abbreviation is placed inside the other word

explanation.surface: Someone takes action just as the court sits.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to take action or perform a deed.

clue.text: Enjoy sage in a similar manner

parts.note: to like something is to enjoy it
a sage person is wise

explanation.surface: Relish a herb in the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like the herb; it is the adjective meaning wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Likewise means similarly, in the same fashion.

clue.text: Recover after oxygen is given by mouth

indicators.note: after says the recover word follows the oxygen symbol

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
to rally is to recover strength or health

explanation.surface: A patient recovers once oxygen is administered by mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking medicine orally means swallowing it, via the mouth.

clue.text: Medieval scribe maybe or advertising executive

explanation.definitionFit: A scribe who duplicated manuscripts was literally one who wrote copies, while in advertising the copy is the promotional text a writer produces.

clue.text: Long day at work for a woman

indicators.note: at work suggests the letters of day being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A long working day for a female employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' rearranges DAY into ADY. 'Long day at work' reads as a complaint about overtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a polite term for a woman.

clue.text: Believer is to stop throwing out son

indicators.note: throwing out signals that the son abbreviation is removed from the word

parts.note: to desist is to stop doing something

explanation.surface: A man of faith is told to quit ejecting his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: One S is dropped from DESIST; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A deist believes in a creator God who does not intervene, a form of religious faith.

clue.text: French wine brought boy over with two ducks for the meal

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: over signals that the word for boy is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, written O, so two give OO

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's wine, a lad and two ducks make a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses LAD to DAL. 'Ducks' suggests birds for the meal; they are zeros.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a hot Indian curry dish, a meal often served in British curry houses.

clue.text: Dorothy's marriage portion

definitions.meaning: the possessive reads as the short form belonging to the woman's name, a pet form

explanation.definitionFit: Dot is a diminutive of the name Dorothy, and also an old word for a dowry brought to a marriage.

clue.text: Press in charge? That's paradoxical

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Is the press in control? How contradictory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests newspapers; it is the household chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ironic is contrary to what one expects, a kind of contradiction.

clue.text: Forge a common name, one unknown

parts.note: Smith is the commonest surname in Britain
Y is one of the letters standing for unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: Fake a widespread surname belonging to a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forge' looks like a verb meaning fake; it is the blacksmith's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy is a blacksmith's workshop, where metal is worked.

clue.text: Parts for example for people in the streets

indicators.note: in signals that the example and people go inside the streets abbreviation

parts.note: ST is street, so STS is streets
EG, exempli gratia, means for example
men are people

explanation.surface: Roles, for instance, for folk out on the roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Segments are divisions or sections of a whole.
